data.title: IRS Shuts Down FIRE Today: What Information Return Filers Need to Know Before the 2027 Filing Season
data.description:
DALLAS, TX AND FAYETTEVILLE, AR / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / The IRS stopped accepting information returns through its Filing Information Returns Electronically (FIRE) system at 3 p.m. ET on November 19, 2026. Beginning with the 2027 filing season, filers must use IRIS to electronically submit tax year 2026 information returns, prior-year returns, and corrections. 

For businesses filing their own information returns and for accounting firms filing on behalf of clients, the change goes well beyond a new login. Anyone who transmitted returns through FIRE directly now needs a new IRIS Transmitter Control Code (TCC), and filing results and corrections now work differently. The transition also arrives alongside the new $2,000 threshold for Form 1099-NEC and certain Form 1099-MISC payments, which leaves little room for a January learning curve.

What changes in the filing workflow? 

IRIS is not FIRE with a new name. Four differences matter most for filers: 

  • Format. FIRE accepted fixed-length files based on IRS Publication 1220. IRIS uses XML-based specifications defined in IRS Publication 5718, so existing FIRE files cannot be submitted to IRIS without conversion. 
  • Credentials. FIRE TCCs are not accepted in IRIS. Anyone transmitting directly to the IRS needs a new IRIS TCC through a separate application process. 
  • Results. IRIS provides record-level acknowledgments with statuses such as Accepted, Accepted with Errors, Partially Accepted, or Rejected. Records accepted with errors are counted as filed, but the IRS expects filers to correct the identified errors. A recipient name and TIN mismatch is a common cause of Accepted with Errors. 
  • Corrections. Corrections can be filed only for records the IRS accepted, with or without errors. Rejected returns are handled as replacements rather than corrections. Because records within the same transmission can receive different statuses, filers need to know which status applies to each record. 

Will you need an IRIS TCC?

A TCC identifies the sender of returns to the IRS, so a filer needs one only if it transmits returns itself. The IRS issues IRIS TCCs to Issuers (businesses filing their own returns), Transmitters (filing on behalf of other businesses), and Software Developers. That leaves two paths: 

  • Transmitting directly to the IRS: the filer needs its own IRIS TCC (as an Issuer for its own returns, or a Transmitter for clients), ID.me identity verification, and a signature from each Responsible Official. The IRS says to allow up to 45 calendar days for the application, so an organization applying now could be waiting into early January. Transmitting from in-house software also requires an API Client ID and IRS testing. 
  • Filing through an authorized e-file provider: the provider transmits under its own TCC, so the filer needs none. 

Tax1099, the IRS-authorized e-filing platform from Zenwork, Inc., falls in the second path. It sends federal returns to IRIS under its own transmitter credentials, so there is no separate IRIS application or transmission process for its users to manage. Users still prepare and approve their filing data. 

What filers should prioritize before January? 

  1. Confirm the filing path for every entity you file for, and whose TCC each one uses. 
  2. Collect missing W-9s and run TIN checks on 2026 payees, so mismatches are fixed before they come back as record-level errors. 
  3. Apply the new $2,000 threshold only where it belongs: Form 1099-NEC and certain Form 1099-MISC payments made in 2026. Other box-specific thresholds are unchanged.
  4. Check state rules, since states may set their own reporting thresholds and filing requirements.
  5. Assign who reviews IRIS results and set an internal deadline well before February 1, 2027, when Form 1099-NEC is due, leaving time to resubmit rejected records. 

How Tax1099 supports the transition

As businesses and accounting firms prepare for the IRS's transition from FIRE to IRIS, one of the most pressing concerns is the conversion of legacy Publication 1220 FIRE files into the new IRIS-compatible format. For organizations with years of historical filing data, manually reformatting files can be both time-consuming and error-prone.

To simplify this process, Tax1099's FIRE-to-IRIS Converter enables users to seamlessly transform existing Publication 1220 FIRE files into IRIS-ready files. Users can review and validate converted records before submission, helping reduce filing errors and accelerate adoption of the new IRS filing framework.

Beyond file conversion, Tax1099 helps organizations simplify every stage of the IRIS transition.

  • IRIS transmission without a TCC: federal returns are sent to IRIS under Tax1099's own credentials, so users do not need to obtain and manage their own IRIS TCC. 
  • Data validation: real-time and bulk TIN Match and USPS address validation before submission. 
  • Bulk import and integrations: Excel or CSV upload and integrations including QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop, Xero, Sage Intacct, Oracle NetSuite, and BILL. 
  • Federal and state in one workflow: filing with the IRS, the SSA, and participating states through the Combined Federal/State Filing (CFSF) program. 
  • Status and corrections in one place: IRIS results and corrections return to the same workflow, and IRS-rejected forms can be resubmitted at no extra cost. 
  • Recipient delivery: IRS-compliant eDelivery with recipient consent tracking, plus print and mail. 

"The move from FIRE to IRIS changes how information returns are filed, tracked, and corrected, and it lands in the same season as the new $2,000 threshold," said Sanjeev Singh, Founder and CEO of Zenwork. "Tax1099 has been filing through IRIS for the past few seasons, so our workflow is already proven, not something we're building for this deadline. Businesses and accounting firms that move to Tax1099 don't have to learn IRIS on their own or apply for their own IRIS credentials. They can validate recipient data, track each record's status, and correct issues in one place, using a process our customers already rely on."

Filers can check where they stand with Tax1099's FIRE Retirement (IRIS) Readiness Checker at tax1099.com/fire-retirement-readiness and review the 2026 changes at tax1099.com/2026changes. 

About Zenwork Tax1099

Supporting 40+ federal and state-compliant forms, including Form 941, Tax1099 offers robust features like bulk filing, API integration, and 24/7 AI assistance, plus live chat and email support. Backed by over 10 years of experience in tax processing and customer service, the platform offers a suite of capabilities to suit diverse needs.

data.title: Newcore Gold Announces Submission of Mining Lease Application for the Enchi Gold Project, Ghana
data.description:
VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Newcore Gold Ltd. ("Newcore" or the "Company") (TSX-V: NCAU, OTCQX: NCAUF) is pleased to announce the submission of a Mining Lease application for the Company's Enchi Gold Project ("Enchi" or the "Project") in Ghana. The Mining Lease application covers 53.37 km2 of the 248 km2 property.

Honourable Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, Minister for Lands & Natural Resources, Ghana stated, "The Government of Ghana welcomes Newcore's submission of a Mining Lease application for the Enchi Gold Project. The Project is one of the most advanced large-scale gold projects in development in Ghana and has the potential to create long-term benefits through job creation, local community support and contribution to national revenues. We support investment that develops our resources responsibly and creates long-term value for Ghanaians, while meeting the highest environmental standards. The Ministry looks forward to working closely with Newcore and the Minerals Commission as the application moves through the review process, with the goal of granting a Mining Lease for the Enchi Gold Project in the first half of 2027."

Luke Alexander, President, CEO and Director of Newcore stated, "The submission of the Mining Lease application is a key step in the permitting process for our Enchi Gold Project in Ghana. It represents the first stage in the permitting path, de-risking and advancing the Project to development-ready status. The Government of Ghana has shown strong support for Enchi, and we look forward to continuing to work with the government, local communities and all stakeholders as we advance the Enchi Gold Project's development path to production."

The Company anticipates that the review process for the Mining Lease application will be completed by mid-2027. Once the mining lease is granted, the Company can formally start its application to the Ghana Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) for an environmental permit. This next step will be supported by environmental monitoring and baseline work that has been on-going at Enchi since 2015, along with environmental and social baseline studies completed for the Project in 2015, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026. The studies completed have concluded that there are no existing issues related to water, soil, noise or air quality for the proposed development of the Project. The most recent studies were completed by Abbakus Geosocial Consult Limited based in Accra, Ghana, an independent group with extensive experience focused on mining projects in Ghana. The Project is looked upon favourably by the local communities and stakeholders and is in an area with a long history of gold exploration, development, and mining.

About Newcore Gold Ltd.
Newcore Gold is advancing its Enchi Gold Project located in Ghana, Africa's largest gold producer (1). Newcore Gold offers investors a unique combination of top-tier leadership, who are aligned with shareholders through their 12% equity ownership, and prime district scale exploration opportunities. Enchi's 248 km2 land package covers 40 kilometres of Ghana's prolific Bibiani Shear Zone, a gold belt which hosts several multi-million-ounce gold deposits, including the Chirano mine 50 kilometres to the north. Newcore's vision is to build a responsive, creative and powerful gold enterprise that maximizes returns for shareholders.
(1) Source: Production volumes for 2025 as sourced from the World Gold Council.

data.title: Americans Believe Affordable and Reliable Electricity Can Be Met by Using Nuclear in Addition to Wind and Solar
data.description:
Americans Believe Affordable and Reliable Electricity Can Be Met by Using Nuclear in Addition to Wind and Solar

The latest ecoAmerica poll shows support for nuclear in addition to wind and solar across political divides. Record high support for next generation nuclear research and development. Americans want data centers to run on clean energy

Americans believe that using nuclear in addition to wind and solar can help provide them with affordable and reliable electricity. About 81 percent of Americans feel that utilizing nuclear power with wind and solar will allow them to have affordable electricity. About 51 percent stated that it was very important to them and 79 percent believe that nuclear power with wind and solar will allow them to have reliable electricity. These results come from ecoAmerica’s ninth annual American Climate Perspectives Survey. This survey follows the views that Americans have on their energy usage and technology decisions.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261119863154/en/

"Americans want affordable electricity and to keep the lights on. Nuclear can work alongside wind and solar to accomplish this. Support for research on next generation nuclear power is at an all time high which allows us to lower costs and continue providing affordable electricity.” Dr. Frank Ling, Chief Scientist at Anthropocene Institute.

Americans of All Political Affiliations Agree on Affordable and Reliable Electricity

Whether you're a Democrat, Republican or Independent eighty four percent feel that nuclear power can provide them with affordable electricity when used with wind and solar. When it comes to having reliable electricity 82 percent of Democrats and 81 percent of Republicans agree that nuclear power can provide them with that. Seventy seven percent of Independents also feel that nuclear power can provide them with reliable electricity.

Americans Support Using Retired Coal Power Plants as Nuclear Power Plants

If we were able to convert retired coal power plants to nuclear power plants that would provide cleaner and more reliable energy 72 percent of Americans would support this. Seventy eight percent of Republicans, 74 percent of Democrats and seventy percent of Independents would support using retired coal plants as nuclear plants.

Data Centers Should Use Clean Energy

Seventy percent of Americans think that data centers should use clean energy to fulfill their electricity needs. Only 13 percent stated that they should not use clean energy. When asked if there should be regulations in place to protect surrounding areas from air, water and soil contamination 82 percent of Americans agreed.

Record High Support for Nuclear Research and Development

Sixty two percent of Americans think we should spend more money on research and development of the next generation of nuclear energy. This number has increased since 2018 and is the highest it has been. In the last year sixty two percent of Republicans now support spending more on research and development. Democrats have also increased from fifty eight to sixty four percent in the past year. Overall support for nuclear has increased by nine points since 2018 and Americans have supported nuclear for all reasons we asked about. Reliability being the highest reason at seventy four percent.

Americans Have Less Concern About Nuclear Except Cost

Since 2018 Americans have had less concerns about nuclear power. Seven percent less are concerned about health and safety risks of nuclear and twelve percent are less concerned about waste disposal. There has been a five point increase in people that are concerned about the cost of nuclear power. We can address this by showing Americans how we can reduce the cost of building new nuclear power plants. A study done by Idaho National Laboratory in 2025 showed that if we could build three additional AP1000's we can begin competing in the US market without any tax incentives.

"ecoAmerica’s latest poll finds that most Americans, across the political spectrum, want data centers to run on clean energy. Nuclear energy seems almost custom-made for this purpose: it provides round-the-clock, carbon-free power with unparalleled reliability. However, Americans have grown increasingly concerned about what it costs. To deliver on nuclear’s promise of cheap, abundant electricity, the industry’s job is to drive down both the cost and the time it takes to build new reactors,” said Madison Hilly, Managing Director at Radiant Energy Group.

Methodology

The survey was conducted online by ecoAmerica among 1,133 US Adults September 1st through September 9th 2026. The margin of error is +/-3 percent. ecoAmerica does not take a stance on Nuclear Energy.

About Anthropocene Institute

Focused on solutions for grid reliability and affordable clean energy for all, Anthropocene Institute supports investments and partnerships that promote nuclear energy for health, wealth, security, and climate repair. Learn more at anthropoceneinstitute.com

Zymeworks is advancing a diverse pipeline of novel biotherapeutics, leveraging its proprietary Azymetric™ platform and expertise in antibody-drug conjugates, multispecific antibodies and other next-generation antibody technologies. data.title: First Atlantic Nickel & Cobalt Attends Critical Minerals Briefing on Capitol Hill, Highlighting New Cerium Refining Technology That Extracted 98% of the Nickel and 82% of the Cobalt From Pipestone XL Awaruite (Ni-Fe-Co Alloy) in 20 Minutes Without Smelting, in Columbia University Research Funded by the U.S. Department of Energy's ARPA-E MINER Program
data.description:
GRAND FALLS-WINDSOR, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- First Atlantic Nickel & Cobalt Corp. (TSXV: FAN) (OTCQB: FANCF) (FSE: P210) ("First Atlantic" or the "Company") is pleased to announce its attendance at the Fastmarkets Critical Minerals and Materials Briefing, taking place today, November 19, 2026, on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC.1 The Company is attending to highlight the new cerium refining technology developed at Columbia University. As reported on November 18, 2026,2 the technology extracted 98% of the nickel and 82% of the cobalt in 20 minutes from awaruite (Ni-Fe-Co alloy) concentrate sourced from the Company's Pipestone XL Nickel-Cobalt Alloy Project, with approximately 90% of the nickel extracted within the first 5 minutes. The process operated at room temperature, with no smelting and no sulfuric acid pretreatment, as reported on November 18, 2026.3

First Atlantic has also launched a new website at www.fanickel.com, featuring an interactive chart of the cerium refining results, drill results and interactive maps of the Pipestone XL Project.

The briefing is being held on Capitol Hill4, and brings together federal policymakers, critical minerals producers and processors, defense and aerospace leaders, investors and industrial buyers to examine the next phase of U.S. critical minerals strategy, including domestic mining, processing and refining capacity. The program includes a fireside chat, "What's Next for Critical Minerals? U.S. Policy Priorities," with U.S. Representatives Gary Palmer and Paul Tonko, Chairman and Ranking Member respectively, of the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Environment. First Atlantic Chief Executive Officer Adrian Smith and Strategic Advisor Dr. Douglas Wicks, former Program Director of the U.S. Department of Energy's ARPA-E MINER program and Geologic Hydrogen portfolio, are attending on behalf of the Company.

Gary Stanley, Strategic Advisor to First Atlantic and former Director of the Office of Critical Minerals and Metals at the U.S. Department of Commerce, is a panelist on "Critical Minerals and U.S. Defense Readiness: Securing Strategic Supply Chains" alongside Jeffrey Frankston, Deputy Assistant Secretary of War for Industrial Base Resilience at the U.S. Department of War.5 First Atlantic welcomes the opportunity to meet with government, defense and industry representatives during the briefing.

First Atlantic is working with Columbia University, its Research Partner, to advance the new breakthrough cerium refining technology developed at Columbia University as a domestic refining option for awaruite (Ni-Fe-Co alloy), a naturally occurring magnetic nickel-iron-cobalt alloy that is concentrated by magnetic separation and flotation without smelting.6 The Columbia University research was funded by the U.S. Department of Energy's ARPA-E MINER program, which was created to increase domestic production of critical minerals such as nickel and cobalt. Nickel sulfide concentrates, by contrast, must be smelted before they can be refined, and only two pyrometallurgical nickel smelters remain in operation in North America, both in Sudbury, Ontario, while the only nickel smelter in the United States, in Riddle, Oregon, closed permanently in 1998.7 Because awaruite does not need a smelter, the Columbia University research indicates strong potential for First Atlantic to develop a vertically integrated, onshore nickel and cobalt supply chain in North America: mining and concentrating awaruite at Pipestone XL in Newfoundland, then shipping a high-grade nickel-cobalt alloy concentrate directly into downstream refining to produce Class 1 nickel metal or nickel sulfate (NiSO₄), without a smelting step.

First Atlantic welcomes direct calls from shareholders and prospective investors. Rob Guzman, Investor Relations, is available at +1-844-592-6337 or by email at rob@fanickel.com to answer questions about this news release or the Company. Because call volume is high, please leave a voice message or email Rob to request a call back.

KEY HIGHLIGHTS

  • Capitol Hill briefing on U.S. critical minerals strategy: First Atlantic is attending the Fastmarkets Critical Minerals and Materials Briefing 2026 in Washington, DC, where Strategic Advisor Gary Stanley is a panelist on "Critical Minerals and U.S. Defense Readiness: Securing Strategic Supply Chains."
  • New cerium refining technology: Columbia University research funded by the U.S. Department of Energy’s ARPA-E MINER program extracted 98% of the nickel and 82% of the cobalt from Pipestone XL awaruite concentrate in 20 minutes, with approximately 90% of the nickel extracted in the first 5 minutes (see Figure 2).
  • Cerium is recycled and reused in the refining loop: The cerium solution works at room temperature and atmospheric pressure, with no sulfuric acid pretreatment. Spent cerium(III) is converted back to cerium(IV) by electrochemical regeneration and reused in the leach in a closed-loop process design (see Figure 3).
  • Awaruite nickel-cobalt alloy outperformed nickel sulfide: Compared with nickel sulfide samples from Tamarack, awaruite yielded up to 66% more nickel extraction in one-third of the time, while the sulfide samples consumed up to 16 times more cerium (see Table 1).
  • High-grade magnetic alloy concentrate with no smelting required: The Company's ONSHORE MAX™ process produced a magnetic alloy concentrate averaging 67.4% nickel, grading up to 71.9% nickel and 1.76% cobalt, compared with 10% to 15% nickel in typical sulfide concentrates.
  • Vertically integrated North American supply chain: Mining and concentrating awaruite in Newfoundland, then refining the alloy concentrate in the United States with cerium refining technology, has the potential to keep nickel and cobalt in North America from mine to refined metal.
  • U.S. government engagement: First Atlantic is a member of the Defense Industrial Base Consortium (DIBC) and has applied under RPP-CM-26-01, "Domestic Processing Capabilities of Critical Minerals," with Columbia University as its Research Partner.
  • New website launched: First Atlantic has launched a new website at www.fanickel.com, featuring an interactive chart of the cerium refining results, drill results and interactive maps of the Pipestone XL Project.

Dr. Douglas Wicks, Strategic Advisor to First Atlantic and former Program Director of the U.S. Department of Energy's ARPA-E MINER program and Geologic Hydrogen portfolio, commented:

"The ARPA-E MINER program was created to develop commercially scalable technologies that increase domestic production of critical minerals such as nickel and cobalt. As its Program Director I funded this Columbia University research, and the results on First Atlantic's awaruite concentrate from Pipestone XL demonstrate the successful test of cerium refining: approximately 98% of the nickel and 82% of the cobalt extracted in 20 minutes, at room temperature, without smelting or sulfuric acid. Because the cerium is regenerated with electricity and reused, the process has the potential to be cost-effective and scalable to commercial production, and to help onshore the refining of Class 1 nickel metal or battery-grade nickel in North America."

Source: graphical abstract, Donovan et al. (2026), ACS Sustainable Resource Management.

NEW CERIUM REFINING TECHNOLOGY: REFINING AWARUITE WITHOUT A SMELTER, AT ROOM TEMPERATURE, WITH NO SULFURIC ACID PRETREATMENT

In Columbia University's new cerium refining technology, the nickel is dissolved (leached) by a cerium salt solution at room temperature and atmospheric pressure, with no heating and no pressure vessel. Two cerium(IV) salts were tested, and both extracted approximately 98% of the nickel from Pipestone XL awaruite concentrate in 20 minutes (97.5% and 98.1%), with no acid pretreatment. That is up to 66% more nickel, extracted in one-third of the time, compared with the Tamarack nickel sulfide samples.

In the study, awaruite achieved higher nickel extraction in less time, with less cerium consumption, than the Tamarack nickel sulfide samples. Under the same conditions, the sulfide samples reached 59% to 82.5% nickel extraction after 60 minutes, and consumed up to 16 times more cerium than awaruite (sample CGO-HM, Table 1). The best sulfide result, 84% (sample SMSU-HM, acid pretreated), was reached only after the sample was first treated with hot sulfuric acid to remove iron sulfide (pyrrhotite); without that pretreatment, the same material reached 70.5% (sample SMSU-HM, no pretreatment).9 Awaruite contains no sulfur, which is why it leaches quickly, consumes little cerium and needs no acid pretreatment.

The cerium is not used up in the process. It works in a closed loop: cerium(IV), the active form, dissolves the nickel and cobalt and is converted to cerium(III), the spent form. An electrochemical cell then uses electricity to convert the cerium(III) back to cerium(IV), which is returned to the leach and reused. Columbia demonstrated multiple cerium regeneration cycles, so the cerium acts as a recyclable carrier and not as a reagent that is consumed.


Figure 2: Nickel extraction over time with the new cerium refining technology. Pipestone XL awaruite concentrate reached approximately 90% nickel extraction in 5 minutes and 98% in 20 minutes, compared with 59% to 82.5% after 60 minutes for the Tamarack nickel sulfide samples in the same Columbia University study. Data from Donovan et al. (2026), ACS Sustainable Resource Management; points between the start and end values are approximate, read from the paper's charts. Chart by First Atlantic.


Figure 3: The cerium closed loop. Cerium(IV) dissolves the nickel and cobalt and is converted to cerium(III); electricity converts the cerium(III) back to cerium(IV), which is reused, at room temperature and atmospheric pressure with no smelter. Diagram by First Atlantic.


Figure 4: First Atlantic Chief Executive Officer Adrian Smith (left) and Strategic Advisor Gary Stanley (right), former Director of the Office of Critical Minerals and Metals at the U.S. Department of Commerce, at the Columbia Electrochemical Energy Center laboratory, Department of Chemical Engineering, Columbia University, in New York, standing in front of the cerium leach solutions and nickel products from Columbia's cerium leaching testwork.

CERIUM: AN ABUNDANT, LOW-COST RARE EARTH PRODUCED BY MP MATERIALS AT MOUNTAIN PASS, CALIFORNIA

Cerium is the most abundant of the rare earth elements, more common in the Earth's crust than copper. It is also one of the cheapest: cerium oxide averaged US$1.71 per kilogram in 2025, according to the U.S. Geological Survey.10 Cerium is produced alongside the magnet rare earths and is in surplus, with one industry estimate placing 2024 output near 167,000 tonnes against demand near 60,000 tonnes, and it is not on China's export control lists.11 In the United States, MP Materials produces cerium chloride as one of four rare earth compounds at Mountain Pass, California,12 which the company describes as the only integrated rare earth site of its kind in the Western Hemisphere.13 In Columbia's process, the cerium is designed to be regenerated with electricity after it dissolves the nickel and returned to the leach for reuse.

THE MIDSTREAM BOTTLENECK: SMELTING CAPACITY AND SULFURIC ACID SUPPLY

Inco's Thompson smelter complex in Manitoba began production in 1961.14 Vale closed the Thompson smelter and refinery on July 31, 2018,15 having been advised that compliance with federal sulphur dioxide regulations would cost approximately $1 billion.16 The only nickel smelter in the United States, at Riddle, Oregon, closed permanently in 1998.17 Only two pyrometallurgical nickel smelters remain in operation in North America, both located in Sudbury, Ontario.18

Conventional nickel refining depends heavily on sulfuric acid, and that dependence was exposed in 2026. The Middle East supplies approximately 25% of the world's sulfur, and 45% to 50% of seaborne sulfur trade moves through the Strait of Hormuz.19 Following the outbreak of conflict in the region on February 28, 2026, the price of sulfur delivered to Indonesia rose from approximately US$563 per tonne to a peak near US$1,300 per tonne,20 and on April 10, 2026 China announced a near-total ban on sulfuric acid exports.21 On March 13, 2026, an article published by the Modern War Institute at West Point warned that the sulfur shortage threatens nickel, cobalt and copper processing and recommended that the U.S. Department of War fund research into non-sulfuric leaching.22

PIPESTONE XL: FIVE AWARUITE ZONES ON A 30-KILOMETER TREND AND A SMELTER-FREE ROUTE TO DOWNSTREAM PROCESSING IN NORTH AMERICA

Pipestone XL is First Atlantic's wholly owned project covering the entire 30-kilometer Pipestone Ophiolite Complex in central Newfoundland. Five zones of awaruite mineralization have been identified along the trend: RPM, Alloy Max, Super Gulp, Atlantic Lake and Chrome Pond. RPM is the most advanced, with drilling outlining magnetically recoverable awaruite over more than 1.2 kilometers of strike and more than 800 meters of width. The Alloy Max target area is approximately 4 kilometers long and up to 1.5 kilometers wide, and every hole assayed there has returned magnetically recoverable nickel.

Awaruite (Ni₃Fe) is a naturally occurring, magnetic nickel-iron-cobalt alloy that contains no sulphur. Electron microprobe analysis of awaruite from the RPM Zone averaged 77.62% nickel and 1.69% cobalt.23 Because the nickel is already in metallic form, it can be concentrated by magnetic separation and flotation without smelting, roasting or high-pressure acid leaching. In initial test work using the Company's ONSHORE MAX™ (Magnetic Alloy eXtraction) process, magnetic separation produced a concentrate grading approximately 1.6% nickel, which flotation upgraded to an alloy concentrate averaging 67.4% nickel and grading up to 71.9% nickel and 1.76% cobalt.24 A typical nickel concentrate grades 10% to 15% nickel, according to the Nickel Institute.25

Figure 5: The Pipestone XL Nickel-Cobalt (Ni-Fe-Co) Alloy Project. Top: 3D view of the 30-kilometer Pipestone XL trend with the Company's magnetic survey draped on terrain, showing the RPM, Alloy Max, Super Gulp, Atlantic Lake and Chrome Pond Zones. Bottom, left to right: bedrock sample (two views) with visible disseminated awaruite, from beneath shallow overburden at an Alloy Max drill pad (April 8, 2026 news release); drill core with visible awaruite, hole XL-26-18 at 32 meters, Alloy Max South (October 13, 2026); photomicrograph of an awaruite grain up to approximately 2,000 microns, hole AN-25-08 at 370 meters, RPM Zone (September 25, 2025). Awaruite grades of 77.62% nickel and 1.69% cobalt are the RPM Zone electron microprobe average (May 21, 2026); the 67.4% nickel concentrate grade is the average of four flotation tests (June 24, 2026).

A magnetic nickel-cobalt (Ni-Fe-Co) alloy concentrate from the Pipestone XL Project has the potential to be a large-scale source of nickel and cobalt for North America. Because the concentrate does not need a smelter, it can bypass the midstream smelting bottleneck and move directly from the mine to battery chemical refining or to stainless steel and specialty alloy production, keeping the supply chain onshore. Pipestone XL has year-round road access, nearby high-voltage transmission and hydroelectric power from the Bay d'Espoir generating station, and is approximately 200 kilometers from Vale's Long Harbour nickel processing plant and Gander International Airport. The Company is also evaluating chromium as a potential co-product and low-carbon Engineered Mineral Hydrogen with VEMA Hydrogen.


Figure 6: The ONSHORE MAX™ (Magnetic Alloy eXtraction) process. Top, left to right, bench-scale test work at SGS Canada Inc. on RPM Zone material: drum separator producing a magnetic concentrate of approximately 1.6% nickel by low-intensity magnetic separation; rougher flotation cell; awaruite alloy concentrate under a magnet. Four flotation tests averaged 67.4% nickel (63.7% to 71.9%), with 1.76% cobalt in the final test (June 24, 2026 news release). Bottom: conceptual mine-to-refinery supply chain for awaruite alloy concentrate with no smelting step.

ABOUT FIRST ATLANTIC NICKEL & COBALT CORP.

First Atlantic Nickel & Cobalt Corp. (TSXV: FAN | OTCQB: FANCF | FSE: P210) is a critical mineral exploration company in Newfoundland and Labrador advancing the wholly owned Pipestone XL Nickel-Cobalt Alloy Project. The project spans the entire 30-kilometer Pipestone Ophiolite Complex, where five zones, RPM, Alloy Max, Super Gulp, Atlantic Lake and Chrome Pond, contain awaruite (Ni₃Fe), a naturally occurring magnetic nickel-iron-cobalt alloy averaging 77.62% nickel and 1.69% cobalt, with no sulphur and no sulphides. Drilling has outlined two large-scale zones of magnetically recoverable nickel at RPM and Alloy Max.

Because awaruite is already a magnetic metal alloy, it can be concentrated by magnetic separation and flotation without smelting, roasting or high-pressure acid leaching. The Company's ONSHORE MAX™ process has produced an alloy concentrate averaging 67.4% nickel and grading up to 71.9% nickel and 1.76% cobalt, and peer-reviewed Columbia University research has extracted 98% of the nickel and 82% of the cobalt from that concentrate in 20 minutes using a new cerium refining technology. The U.S. Geological Survey noted in 2012 that awaruite is much easier to concentrate than pentlandite, the principal sulphide of nickel.

Pipestone XL has year-round road access, nearby high-voltage transmission and hydroelectric power. First Atlantic has signed a letter of intent with VEMA Hydrogen for a proposed joint venture to develop low-carbon Engineered Mineral Hydrogen at Pipestone XL, and is evaluating chromium as a potential co-product. The Company also holds the Ophiolite-X and North Arm projects in western Newfoundland, and is a member of the U.S. Defense Industrial Base Consortium. Newfoundland and Labrador has ranked among the top 10 jurisdictions worldwide for investment attractiveness or mining policy in every Fraser Institute Annual Survey of Mining Companies since 2022.

data.title: Alibaba Earnings Rebound Sharply as AI Profitability Improves
data.description:
By Tracy Qu

Alibaba Group recorded a surge in fiscal second-quarter profit as its AI profitability and e-commerce business improved.

The Hangzhou-based company has doubled down on artificial intelligence as a growth driver, a push that faces a new risk from heightened scrutiny about exports of chips to China. It has committed to spending more than $53 billion over three years to develop both the hardware and software that power AI.

Its success on that front holds the key to staying competitive amid challenges from other big tech firms and startups alike. But going all in on AI has proved a drag on profitability over recent quarters, putting pressure on Alibaba to deliver on its AI goals.

Its latest results look reassuring.

On Thursday, Alibaba said net profit tripled from a year earlier to 64.535 billion yuan, equivalent to $9.68 billion, for the three months ended September. Analysts polled by FactSet had expected 23.72 billion yuan. Revenue grew about 10% to 271.52 billion yuan, also better than market estimates.

Alibaba attributed the sharp profit improvement to higher net investment income and income from operations.

The earnings beat comes as Alibaba prepares a Hong Kong listing for its chip unit, T-Head, that investors view as a major validation of its efforts to produce in-house semiconductors. The business could fetch a valuation of $85 billion, according to Nomura estimates.

Write to Tracy Qu at tracy.qu@wsj.com

data.title: Ecceamerica Brings European Excellence to Canada: Organic EVO Oil Takes Center Stage in Toronto
data.description:
Ecceamerica Brings European Excellence to Canada: Organic EVO Oil Takes Center Stage in Toronto

From November 12 to 25, 2026, tastings and promotional activities at selected restaurants and retail outlets in Toronto and Oakville will showcase European extra virgin olive oil and the value of organic certification.

The quality of extra virgin olive oil begins long before it reaches the table. Cultivation practices, harvesting and processing techniques all help shape its aromas, intensity and flavor. Italy’s olive-growing biodiversity is particularly rich, with 743 olive varieties listed in the National Register of Fruit Tree Varieties, reflecting a longstanding connection between the land, agricultural traditions and quality production.

Organic certification adds another important dimension. It confirms compliance with European standards for organic production and processing, supports environmentally conscious production methods and helps consumers recognize products that meet specific requirements.

These values are central to Ecceamerica, a project promoted by Unaprol – the Italian Olive Consortium and CAP – Confederação dos Agricultores de Portugal, co-financed by the European Union under Regulation (EU) No. 1144/2014. The three-year program promotes European agri-food excellence in the United States and Canada, with a focus on organic extra virgin olive oil and organic wine. Through information and promotional activities, it aims to strengthen awareness and recognition of these products in both markets.

In Canada, from November 12 to 25, extra virgin olive oil will be featured in a series of tastings and promotional initiatives at selected restaurants and retail outlets in Toronto and Oakville. Visitors will have the opportunity to discover the product’s distinctive characteristics, explore its quality and learn more about the value of European organic production.

Specially trained personnel will guide the tastings and answer questions about extra virgin olive oil, including its characteristics and organic production methods. Dedicated informational materials will also be provided to help consumers better understand the product and make informed choices.

The activities are designed not only to offer a tasting experience, but also to create opportunities for direct dialogue about origin, production standards and everyday use.

By bringing European extra virgin olive oil directly to Canadian consumers, Ecceamerica seeks to highlight its quality, strengthen its recognition and encourage greater familiarity with organic certification.

Detailed schedules for participating restaurants and retail locations will be available on the project website.

For more information and updates, visit https://ecceamerica.eu/ and follow Ecceamerica on Facebook and Instagram.

ORLANDO, FL / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / LASE Corp. (NASDAQ:LASE), an emerging laser technology company developing laser and directed-energy solutions for the defense, pharmaceutical, semiconductor and industrial markets ("LASE" or the "Company"), today announced that it will premiere its Quantum Bullet™ anti-drone platform at Counter Unmanned Aircraft System ("UAS") Technology USA, taking place November 30 through December 2, 2026, in Washington, D.C., where Dmitri Nikitin, Executive Chairman of LASE Corp., will also present as a featured speaker.

This event brings together military, government and industry leaders to address the rapidly evolving threat posed by unmanned aerial systems and the technologies being developed to defeat them. This year's conference speakers include senior representatives of Joint Interagency Task Force 401 (JIATF-401), the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering, the U.S. Army, the Air Force Research Laboratory, U.S. Northern Command and the Department of Homeland Security. Last year's conference drew attendees from more than a dozen countries, NATO, and allied ministries of defense, as well as leading defense contractors.

This premiere complements the Company's previously announced introduction of Quantum Bullet™ at the Interservice/Industry Training, Simulation and Education Conference (I/ITSEC), taking place November 30 through December 3, 2026, in Orlando, Florida.

The Quantum Bullet™ product line includes the Company's Laser Shield Anti-Drone ("LSAD") Series, a modular directed-energy platform being developed to address Group 1 and Group 2 drone threats. LSAD is designed to combine proprietary laser-based counter-drone capabilities with multi-sensor detection, tracking, targeting and command-and-control ("C2") systems supplied by LASE and its integration partners, supporting either standalone deployment or integration into multilayered air-defense networks.

LASE is developing LSAD as a modular offering that can be configured with different laser and power capabilities for different tactical scenarios. Its Dazzler configuration is intended to disrupt the optical and LIDAR sensors of Group 1 and Group 2 drones, while higher-energy palletized and crawler configurations, the latter designed for rapid all-terrain deployment, are being developed for destructive engagement of drone threats. Development, integration, testing and customer evaluation remain necessary before commercialization.

Dmitri Nikitin, Executive Chairman of LASE Corp said, "What we have developed with Quantum Bullet™ is a fundamentally different approach to counter-drone defense. It is designed to deliver the precision, effectiveness and cost efficiency needed to address one of the military's most urgent and widespread threats: Group 1 and Group 2 drones. But what makes Quantum Bullet™ particularly compelling is its versatility. It is not simply a standalone weapon. It is a modular, mobile and integrated defense platform designed to operate independently or as part of a larger, layered defense system."

Dmitri Nikitin continued, "We believe the future of counter-drone defense will depend on technologies that work together, adapt to evolving threats and can be deployed wherever our military needs them. That is exactly what we are building with Quantum Bullet™.

Mr. Nikitin, the Company's founder, brings more than three decades of experience in laser technology innovation spanning marking, cutting, welding, cleaning, glass separation and semiconductor processing. He co-developed the world's first high-power fiber laser cutting system and developed a first-of-its-kind mobile fiber-laser platform for military mine-clearing applications. Mr. Nikitin holds an engineering degree in industrial electronics and quantum mechanics from Moscow Power Engineering University and a Ph.D. from the Ministry of Electronics Industry of the USSR, and he is a named inventor on three patent applications relating to Bulk-to-Shape technology.

Quantum Bullet™ is a registered trademark with the USPTO.

For more information on LASE Corp. and its brands, please visit www.lase.com.

About LASE Corp.

LASE Corp. (NASDAQ:LASE), formerly Laser Photonics Corporation, is an emerging laser technology company developing laser and directed-energy solutions for the defense, pharmaceutical, semiconductor and industrial markets. Through internal development, strategic acquisitions and partnerships, LASE intends to expand its technology portfolio, strengthen its advanced manufacturing capabilities and scale the enterprise profitably.

data.title: ROBOTERA Invited to APEC CEO Summit for Second Consecutive Year, Showcases Real-World Humanoid Robot Applications
data.description:
ROBOTERA Invited to APEC CEO Summit for Second Consecutive Year, Showcases Real-World Humanoid Robot Applications

ROBOTERA Invited to APEC CEO Summit for Second Consecutive Year, Showcases Real-World Humanoid Robot Applications

PR Newswire

BEIJING, Nov. 19, 2026

BEIJING, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ROBOTERA, an AI-native embodied intelligence company, was invited to the 2026 APEC CEO Summit for the second consecutive year, becoming the only embodied intelligence company focused on real-world productivity to receive consecutive invitations. Founder and CEO Jianyu Chen and Co-founder Yue Xi attended the summit . Chen also delivered a keynote speech at APEC Finance Night titled "Putting Robots to Work at Night," sharing ROBOTERA's experience in turning embodied intelligence into practical productivity through real-world logistics deployments.

ROBOTERA has established deployments with China Post and SF Express, with its humanoid robots now operating across over 10 logistics centers. In these real-world operations, the robots achieve parcel induction rates exceeding 1,500 parcels per hour. By taking on repetitive, physically demanding tasks and challenging night shifts, they help address labor shortages while enabling human workers to focus on tasks requiring greater flexibility and judgment.

At the APEC CEO Summit, held from November 17 to 19, ROBOTERA showcased its humanoid robots and logistics solutions, including live parcel sorting demonstrations by its M7 humanoid robot. The demonstration gave international business leaders and attendees a firsthand look at how embodied intelligence is moving beyond technical demonstrations to deliver tangible value in real-world logistics operations.
